Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From French appartement, Italian appartamento, Spanish/Portuguese apartamento; compare Italian appartare (“to separate, set apart”), from Latin ad + pars (“part”) + -amentum.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /apartaˈmento/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ento
  • Syllabification: a‧par‧ta‧men‧to

Noun

[edit]

apartamento (accusative singular apartamenton, plural apartamentoj, accusative plural apartamentojn)

  1. apartment, flat
    Synonym: ĉambraro

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

< Spanish apartamento

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɑpɑrtɑmento/, [ˈɑ̝pɑ̝rt̪ɑ̝ˌme̞n̪t̪o̞]
  • Rhymes: -ento
  • Syllabification(key): a‧par‧ta‧men‧to
  • Hyphenation(key): apar‧ta‧men‧to

Noun

[edit]

apartamento

  1. apartment, especially one in Spain

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English apartment, French appartement, German Appartement, Italian appartamento, Russian апартаме́нт (apartamént), Spanish apartamento.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /apartaˈmento/

Noun

[edit]

apartamento (plural apartamenti)

  1. apartment, flat

Derived terms

[edit]
  • apartamentano (“roommate, flatmate”)

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
apartamento
Wikipedia pt

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • apto. (abbreviation)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian appartamento, possibly through French appartement and/or Spanish apartamento. Ultimately from Spanish apartamiento (“separation, seclusion”), from apartar (“to separate”). By surface analysis, apartar +‎ -mento.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.paʁ.taˈmẽ.tu/ [a.pah.taˈmẽ.tu]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.paʁ.taˈmẽ.tu/ [a.pah.taˈmẽ.tu]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /a.paɾ.taˈmẽ.tu/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /a.paʁ.taˈmẽ.tu/ [a.paχ.taˈmẽ.tu]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /a.paɻ.taˈmẽ.tu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /a.paʁ.taˈmẽ.to/ [a.pah.taˈmẽ.to]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɐ.pɐɾ.tɐˈmẽ.tu/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)); [ɐ.pɐɾ.tɐˈmjẽⁿ.tu]:(file)
  • Hyphenation: a‧par‧ta‧men‧to

Noun

[edit]

apartamento m (plural apartamentos)

  1. flat, apartment

Derived terms

[edit]
  • apê

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
apartamento
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian appartamento, from Spanish apartamiento.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /apaɾtaˈmento/ [a.paɾ.t̪aˈmẽn̪.t̪o]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ento
  • Syllabification: a‧par‧ta‧men‧to

Noun

[edit]

apartamento m (plural apartamentos)

  1. flat, apartment
    Synonyms: (Spain) piso, (Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Peru) departamento, (rare or dialectal) apartamiento

Further reading

[edit]
  • “apartamento”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish apartamento, from Italian appartamento, from Spanish apartamiento (“separation, seclusion”). Doublet of apartment.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ʔapaɾtaˈmento/ [ʔɐ.pɐɾ.t̪ɐˈmɛn̪.t̪o]
  • Rhymes: -ento
  • Syllabification: a‧par‧ta‧men‧to

Noun

[edit]

apartamento (Baybayin spelling ᜀᜉᜇ᜔ᜆᜋᜒᜈ᜔ᜆᜓ)

  1. apartment (domicile occupying part of a building)
    Synonyms: bahay-paupahan, apartment, aksesorya, posesyon
